newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mossgas pumps first condensate from satellite well.
newsitem.headline: Mossgas pumps first condensate from satellite well.

text.p: South Africa's fuel-from-gas producer Mossgas started pumping the first gas and condensates from its offshore satellite fields to the onshore plant at Mossel Bay on Thursday.
Chief executive David Day said in a statement that the flow rates from the first well to be tapped exceeded expectations.
"We are confident that the other three wells, which will be completed over the next three months, will yield equally good results," he said.
The well, FAH4, is 16 km from Mossgas' offshore production platform, which is 85km south of Mossel Bay, and extends 2.4 km below the ocean floor.

It is the first of four wells to be brought into production as part of a 910 million rand offshore programme to extend the life of Mossgas, and is expected to yield a net return of three billion rand.

The programme, which includes the installation of a compression module on the FA platform, will enable Mossgas to maintain its current levels from the FA fields of more than 30,000 barrels of liquid fuels a day until 2001.
This is equal to nearly five million litres, or 45,000 barrels of crude oil, and will save South Africa more than 1.3 billion rand in imports at present prices and exchange rates, Mossgas said.
"The satellite fields project and the compression project, which is due for completion in July 1998, are on schedule as well as on target for completion within budget," Day said.
The approval of the project was delayed until mid-1996 while government attempted, without success, to find a buyer for Mossgas.

Day said the delay had resulted in "extremely tight" schedules as the new wells had to be brought into production in time to ensure a continued supply of gas as the pressure in the main FA field reached a plateau.
Three of the new wells are in the satellite FAH field and one in the FAR field.

Day said that contracts had been awarded to two international companies, Kvaerner Oil & Gas and Dresser Enterprises, to do the design work on the next phase of Mossgas' feedstock development programme.
This would involve the exploitation of the EM field, which was 49 km west of the FA platform. This field had enough reserves to meet Mossgas' needs for a further five years.
